clinicalPearls: Renal osteodystrophy is the bone component of chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD), spanning a spectrum from high-turnover to low-turnover bone disease.
It is driven by phosphate retention, reduced 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, hypocalcaemia, FGF23 excess and secondary hyperparathyroidism.

High-turnover disease (osteitis fibrosa cystica) results from secondary and tertiary hyperparathyroidism, whereas low-turnover forms are adynamic bone disease and, historically, osteomalacia from aluminium or vitamin D deficiency.
Adynamic bone disease is increasingly common with over-suppression of PTH, diabetes and peritoneal dialysis, and carries fracture and vascular calcification risk.

Bone histomorphometry using the turnover-mineralisation-volume (TMV) classification after tetracycline labelling is the gold standard; PTH and bone-specific alkaline phosphatase serve as surrogate markers.
Management targets phosphate control (dietary restriction and phosphate binders), correction of vitamin D deficiency, active vitamin D analogues and calcimimetics for hyperparathyroidism.
Vascular and soft-tissue calcification is a major consequence, so excessive calcium load and over-suppression of turnover should be avoided.
Parathyroidectomy is indicated for severe refractory tertiary hyperparathyroidism, calciphylaxis or intractable symptoms.
reference.pathophysiology: As renal function declines, phosphate excretion falls and FGF23 rises to maintain phosphate balance, while reduced functioning renal mass lowers 1-alpha-hydroxylase activity and hence calcitriol. Falling calcitriol and calcium, together with hyperphosphataemia, stimulate parathyroid hyperplasia and PTH secretion (secondary hyperparathyroidism); persistent stimulation can lead to autonomous tertiary hyperparathyroidism. High PTH increases osteoclastic and osteoblastic activity, producing high-turnover osteitis fibrosa cystica with marrow fibrosis. Conversely, over-suppression of PTH, skeletal PTH resistance, aluminium or diabetes can produce low-turnover adynamic bone. The disordered mineral milieu also promotes ectopic vascular and soft-tissue calcification.
additionalInvestigations: serum calcium, phosphate, PTH and bone-specific alkaline phosphatase
radiographs for subperiosteal resorption and rugger-jersey spine
bone biopsy with double tetracycline labelling in uncertainty
redFlags: rapidly rising PTH suggesting autonomous gland activity
reference.prognosis: The disorder is chronic and progresses with declining renal function; it is controllable with CKD-MBD management but is associated with increased fracture risk and cardiovascular mortality.
pitfalls: relying on DXA alone, which cannot distinguish high- from low-turnover disease
over-suppressing PTH and inducing adynamic bone disease
using excessive calcium-containing binders and promoting vascular calcification
treating biochemistry without regard to the underlying bone-turnover state
references: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline on CKD-MBD
